claims.sourceText: Bolender memorandum, 20 Oct 1969, scan in the NICAP document archive (file 1969_10_20_Bolender_Memo.pdf)
claims.text: A memorandum dated 20 October 1969 by Brig. Gen. C. H. Bolender recommending termination of Project Blue Book exists and is preserved in scanned form in the public record.
The Bolender memorandum of 20 October 1969 states that UFO reports which could affect national security are made under JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and are not part of the Blue Book system.

edges.label: Memo recommended termination; Blue Book closed two months later
edges.note: Secretary of the Air Force Robert C. Seamans Jr. announced the termination on 17 December 1969, citing the Condon Report.

edges.label: Bolender authored the termination memorandum
edges.note: Brig. Gen. Bolender, USAF Deputy Director of Development, signed the 20 October 1969 memorandum recommending Blue Book's closure and explaining why closure cost the Air Force nothing operationally.

edges.label: Bolender names JANAP 146 as the channel Blue Book was not
edges.note: The memorandum states national-security UFO reports are made under JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and are not part of the Blue Book system — an official concession that the public program was never the collection channel.

edges.label: JANAP created a parallel reporting channel outside Blue Book
edges.note: JANAP 146(C) made UFO sightings a mandatory CIRVIS report under espionage-statute penalties while Blue Book handled the public-facing residue. Bolender confirmed the split in 1969.

edges.label: The public statistics are the residue of a filter, not the corpus
edges.note: If national-security reports went up the JANAP channel as Bolender states, then the 12,618 sightings and 701 unknowns describe only what the filtered public program retained.
